stories.title: Diesel’s desire: an engine for everyone
stories.summary: For someone who wished to build an engine for everyone, August turned out to be an auspicious month. On August 10, 1893, Rudolf Diesel’s prime model was powered on its own for the first time. Five years later, on August 9, 1898, Diesel obtained a U.S. patent titled “Internal-combustion engine”. Join A.S.Ganesh as he tries to explain what fuelled Diesel’s desire…

stories.title: Typhoon Saudel makes landfalls on China’s eastern coast, disrupts travel
stories.summary: Typhoon Saudel made two landfalls on China’s eastern coast on Aug 28, as the authorities evacuated people and halted trains and ferries. The typhoon made landfall at the city of Taizhou around 8.05am and the city of Wenzhou around 9.10am, according to state media, marking the third typhoon to strike the eastern province of Zhejiang in 2026. Saudel is set to bring heavy rain to Zhejiang and Fujian, a province on the south-east coast, with possibilities of local torrential downpours, state-run Xinhua news agency reported. As the typhoon moves inland, it could drench provincial-level regions including Hubei, Guangxi and Yunnan. The Wenzhou government ordered the evacuation of more than 820,000 people, while Taizhou authorities suspended eight passenger ferry routes and identified 52,000 people needing evacuation, state broadcaster CCTV reported. Rail operator China Railway Shanghai Group temporarily suspended some services on several lines in Zhejiang from Aug 27 to 28, according to CCTV.

stories.title: Uganda's King of Tooro, once world's youngest reigning monarch, dies at 34
stories.summary: King Oyo Nyimba, leader of the Tooro kingdom in western Uganda, has died at the age of 34, the region's prime minister of his kingdom announced Thursday. Crowned at three years old, he became the world's youngest reigning monarch in 1995.

stories.title: Nepal flash floods: 'Very challenging' for survivors who have lost their homes and their families
stories.summary: Alison Sargent is pleased to welcome Sunita Sharma, Head of Programs of Karuna-Shechen. While Nepal has considerable experience responding to natural disasters, the scale of the present devastation exposes a deeper challenge: Placing greater emphasis on preparedness. The immediate priorities are clear: finding those still missing and providing survivors with drinking water, food, shelter, clothing and medicine. But recovery cannot end there. Ultimately, they will need to rebuild confidence and entire communities. Given the scale of the destruction, that process could take years.

stories.title: Russia, US agree to continue developing business, humanitarian ties
stories.summary: Anton Kobyakov and Robert Agee discussed the further development of Russian-American dialogue and the participation of US representatives in international events organized by the Roscongress Foundation in Russia and abroad
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 28.

Russia and the United States have agreed to continue working to develop business and humanitarian ties, as well as prepare for the participation of US representatives in upcoming international events, the Roscongress Foundation said following a meeting between Anton Kobyakov, Adviser to the President of the Russian Federation, and Robert Agee, President and CEO of the American Chamber of Commerce in Russia (AmCham Russia).

"The parties discussed the further development of Russian-American dialogue and the participation of US representatives in international events organized by the Roscongress Foundation in Russia and abroad," the statement said.

The parties discussed the further development of the Russian-US dialogue and the participation of US representatives in international events organized by the Roscongress Foundation in Russia and abroad, the statement noted.

Potential areas of cooperation include US participation in the Verona Eurasian Economic Forum in Istanbul, the 12th St. Petersburg International Forum of United Cultures and the 6th Congress of Young Scientists.
The participants also paid particular attention to the development of humanitarian ties between the two countries.
"The dialogue between Russia and the United States continues.
The business and cultural sessions at SPIEF 2026 showed that there is a strong appetite on both sides for direct professional engagement.
What matters now is to sustain that momentum and broaden the agenda to include culture, science, and education.
The participation of our American colleagues in international events will allow us to strengthen contacts and move forward with new joint initiatives," Kobyakov said, as quoted in the statement.
Agee thanked the Roscongress Foundation for organizing SPIEF 2026 and holding two Russia-US dialogues, one focused on business and the other on culture.
He also emphasized the American Chamber of Commerce’s interest in continuing these formats.

stories.title: Kremlin denies new Putin-Trump talks
stories.summary: Dmitry Peskov specified that the Donald Trump's statements about holding "good talks" with Vladimir Putin refered to leaders' previous contacts
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 28.
No new talks have been held between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US leader Donald Trump, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
"This refers to previous contacts," Peskov told the Yunashev Live Telegram channel.
Speaking to reporters at the White House on Thursday, Trump said that he had held "good talks" with Putin and expressed confidence that Russia does not plan to attack NATO countries.
